Register against recommended settings

E repeated at the AIRSPEED_MIN and TKOFF_THR_MAX of the FT optimum (D re-run at that entry speed). The register case is the headline above. The last two columns are information only. e_fwd_kJ is E's forward transition: the quasi-steady wait to AIRSPEED_MIN plus the rotor fade of Q_TRANSITION_MS (the rotors fade from the throttle that carries the share of the weight the wing does not, E.fade_wing_share). ft_site_energy_kJ is the mean energy of FT's simulated transition (hover to the end of the fade) over the FT members nearest to that site in the same case, with its wait and fade parts and the member count; e_fwd_over_ft is E divided by it. The members of a group still differ in mass, ISA, headwind and SoC and in altitude by up to about 1 km, so the ratio is a like-for-like size check by site, not a validation.

Energy against stopping distance

C: ensemble mean energy against the 95th-percentile distance, the optimum's ramp with q varied (each point is labelled with its q). B1's scenario points are in the B1 chapter.

C: the optimum's ramp, q varied (hollow = a member is flagged)C register (q = 2)ArduPilot defaultC optimum

What this result rests on

alpha_s = 15.70 deg is a placeholder (the CFD shows no lift peak up to 15 deg), and the blend sharpness M = 70 1/rad is a numerical parameter that also sets C_L,max (1.444, at alpha_w = 13.43 deg): the size of the stall effect, and so the enforced result, is provisional. The rotor model has constant thrust and torque coefficients and no in-plane force (CT1, CT2, CQ1, CQ2, CH1 and k_mu are zero in the register): thrust does not change with airspeed and the rotors add no drag in forward flight.

The enforced configuration and the unconstrained reference

C twice: the wing held to the limit (the headline, written to the recommended settings) and not held (the model's lift falls from its peak to about a third within a few degrees, so the unconstrained optimum flies through the stall). The exposure columns are the worst member (the least wing share is the lowest over members); they are not penalised and not failure flags. Holding the wing below the limit costs 1.87 x the energy, 1.88 x the stopping distance and 1.98 x the stopping time of the unconstrained search; q is 1.07 against 2.03 m/s^2.

Where the default fails (ensemble member 21)

Ensemble member 21: altitude 4680.64 m, ISA +18.3 K, mass 21.6 kg, SoC 0.48, headwind -4.95 m/s, entry airspeed 19.7 m/s true, 15.0 m/s equivalent. The default overshoots this member by 61.65 m and the optimum by 0.18 m.

Worst overshoot and worst end sink against q

The optimum's other three values fixed; q varied. A hollow mark has a failing member.

coarse curve (hollow: a member fails)fine gridoptimummargin row (reported, not recommended)

worst overshoot

worst end sink

The optimum relies on the overshoot and end-sink tolerances, which are PROPOSED, not on a measured limit. At the optimum the margins are 0.21 m and 1.75 m/s. From q = 2.5 the energy, the distance and the end sink do not change with q (0.20 m/s): the pitch is at its ceiling for the whole run, so the run is the same whatever q is; only the overshoot, which is read against the target v^2 / (2 q), keeps growing. The pitch ramp can deliver 1.21 m/s^2 for the weakest member and 1.48 for the strongest (`a_cap_ms2`).

Search convergence

Best cost found by each seed; the spread of these is the T-12 check.

The seeds disagree on J (spread 1.26%, the limit is 1%): the search has not converged.

Ensemble spread

One strip per metric, one dot per member; the ArduPilot default's members are the hollow grey dots below each strip.

member of the optimumflagged membermember of the ArduPilot defaulttolerance (PROPOSED)

No member of the optimum stops short of the target: the overshoot is positive in all 32 and ranges from 0.17 to 1.79 m. The end sink is at most 0.01 m/s. The stop target assumes the planned deceleration q from t = 0, while the pitch ramp over T_bt delays the braking, so the aircraft stops past it.

One-at-a-time sensitivity

One setting changes at a time. The change of the full J is dominated by the failure penalty, so the figure shows the failures and the smooth part of J apart; x marks a row where members fail (the tooltip has the expressions).

What the gap between B1 and C contains

S-01: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 18.0 kJ over 83 m. B1 `margin` needs 14.2 kJ (21 % less): it flies the same wing limit and the same pitch ceiling (20 deg), so the pitch freedom is already removed from that saving; what is left is B1's missing rotor lag (C has 0.25 s) and its clairvoyance (B1 knows the scenario and is open loop, where C's four settings serve every ensemble member). B1 `attached` needs 11.1 kJ (-3.1 kJ against `margin`, 38 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 13.34 deg, and a pitch command above C's ceiling). B1 `c_envelope` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. C without the wing cap needs 16.0 kJ over 58 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. S-02: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 29.4 kJ over 138 m. B1 `margin` needs 22.9 kJ (22 % less): it flies the same wing limit and the same pitch ceiling (20 deg), so the pitch freedom is already removed from that saving; what is left is B1's missing rotor lag (C has 0.25 s) and its clairvoyance (B1 knows the scenario and is open loop, where C's four settings serve every ensemble member). B1 `attached` needs 18.1 kJ (-4.8 kJ against `margin`, 38 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 13.34 deg, and a pitch command above C's ceiling). B1 `c_envelope` needs 18.0 kJ (-4.9 kJ against `margin`, 39 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 30.00 deg). C without the wing cap needs 27.4 kJ over 95 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. S-03: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 39.9 kJ over 140 m. B1 `margin` needs 29.4 kJ (26 % less): it flies the same wing limit and the same pitch ceiling (20 deg), so the pitch freedom is already removed from that saving; what is left is B1's missing rotor lag (C has 0.25 s) and its clairvoyance (B1 knows the scenario and is open loop, where C's four settings serve every ensemble member). B1 `attached` needs 22.9 kJ (-6.5 kJ against `margin`, 43 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 13.34 deg, and a pitch command above C's ceiling). B1 `c_envelope` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. C without the wing cap needs 35.7 kJ over 98 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. S-04: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 32.9 kJ over 136 m. B1 `margin` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. B1 `attached` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. B1 `c_envelope` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. C without the wing cap needs 32.8 kJ over 106 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. S-05: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 11.7 kJ over 44 m. B1 `margin` needs 7.6 kJ (35 % less): it flies the same wing limit and the same pitch ceiling (20 deg), so the pitch freedom is already removed from that saving; what is left is B1's missing rotor lag (C has 0.25 s) and its clairvoyance (B1 knows the scenario and is open loop, where C's four settings serve every ensemble member). B1 `attached` needs 6.1 kJ (-1.6 kJ against `margin`, 48 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 13.34 deg, and a pitch command above C's ceiling). B1 `c_envelope` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. C without the wing cap needs 9.4 kJ over 31 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. S-06: C (register parameters, q = 2, wing held to 10.99 deg) needs 19.4 kJ over 143 m. B1 `margin` needs 15.0 kJ (23 % less): it flies the same wing limit and the same pitch ceiling (20 deg), so the pitch freedom is already removed from that saving; what is left is B1's missing rotor lag (C has 0.25 s) and its clairvoyance (B1 knows the scenario and is open loop, where C's four settings serve every ensemble member). B1 `attached` needs 11.7 kJ (-3.3 kJ against `margin`, 40 % below C): it adds operation at the lift peak (|alpha_w| up to 13.34 deg, and a pitch command above C's ceiling). B1 `c_envelope` has no verified point here, so nothing is said about it. C without the wing cap needs 17.1 kJ over 95 m because the model ignores the stall: a reference, not a competitor. So the B1-C gap is not what a better ArduPilot parameter set could save: it is the sum of the missing rotor lag, the clairvoyance and, for `attached` and `c_envelope`, the lift-peak operation.

Is "margin" flyable?

The margin limit is |alpha_w| <= 10.99 deg (0.70 x alpha_s, alpha_s = 15.70 deg). The model's C_L peaks at alpha_w = 13.43 deg (C_L,max 1.444), in the same convention. The limit sits 2.44 deg below that peak, where C_L is 90.55% of C_L,max. That is a margin in angle before the lift peak. The replayed peak wing angle of the verified points is 11.00 to 11.08 deg.

Is "attached" attached?

The attached limit is |alpha_w| <= 13.34 deg (0.85 x alpha_s, alpha_s = 15.70 deg). The model's C_L peaks at alpha_w = 13.43 deg (C_L,max 1.444), in the same convention. The limit sits 0.09 deg below that peak, where C_L is 99.98% of C_L,max. It leaves no stall margin in lift: the wing is flown at the top of the lift curve, not below it. The replayed peak wing angle of the verified points is 13.34 to 13.39 deg.

Wing share at the hand-over

Share of the weight the wing carries when the pusher takes over (1 would be the whole weight), one strip per case and one dot per member. Within a case the hand-over speed is the setting, so the dots differ by the wing share only.

Cost against Q_TRANSITION_MS

The best snapped cost found with Q_TRANSITION_MS fixed at each value (the other three searched, then snapped to ArduPilot's integers). The winner is marked; a hollow mark is a point whose snapped optimum still has flagged members, none here; a square is a point whose three-seed spread is above the T-12 limit, none here. Over the 15 grid points J runs from 0.759 (Q_TRANSITION_MS 17 s) to 0.878 (2 s), 15.7% above the lowest. At the register's Q_TRANSITION_MS (5 s) J is 0.839, +10.6% against the winner's. 5 of 15 points lie within the seed spread (0.39%) of the best: Q_TRANSITION_MS 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17 s. The whole range is 0.4% of what re-tuning all four settings gains from the register start (J 31.30 to 0.759), so with the other three re-tuned the fade length is a second-order choice. Within 2 % of the best cost: Q_TRANSITION_MS 14, 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17, 20 s.

Final cost by seed

The cost each search seed ended at, with that seed's four settings in the tooltip. It is the end point of the seed, not its path: iteration data is not stored, so convergence itself is not shown.

One-at-a-time sensitivity

Absolute change of the cost J against the base evaluation (J = 0.7588) when one setting changes; a row shows its failing-member count. The axis is linear within the seed spread of zero and logarithmic beyond it, so the one large row does not flatten the others. The seed spread is 0.39% of J, 0.0030 in J. Apart from C_L,max, these inputs DO move J by more than that: TECS_TIME_CONST = 3.0 (-0.118, 0 failing), TECS_TIME_CONST = 8.0 (+0.186, 0 failing), TECS_INTEG_GAIN = 0.15 (+0.166, 0 failing), TECS_INTEG_GAIN = 0.6 (-0.149, 0 failing), rotor_lag_s = 0.0 (-0.005, 0 failing), rotor_lag_s = 0.5 (+0.005, 0 failing), z_vel_p = 2.5 (+0.020, 0 failing), z_vel_p = 10.0 (-0.012, 0 failing), TRIM_THROTTLE = 0.35 (+0.092, 0 failing), TRIM_THROTTLE = 0.55 (-0.043, 0 failing), tecs_start = cold (+0.055, 0 failing).

Notes

FT_params, FT_runs and FT_history evaluate the optimum, the register start and the ArduPilot default on the first 32 members of the Sobol sample and the 8 corners. The grid search, FT_grid, FT_sens and J_start use the first 16 members. The optimum is the best snapped point of FT_grid: whole m/s, whole degrees, whole percent and whole milliseconds, the values ArduPilot can take.

FT_robust and the optimum_robust row of FT_params are evaluated on the first 16 members, the ensemble of the sensitivities, and are reported only: no search, never the recommendation.

T-12 on the grid: 15 of 15 points have a three-seed spread within 1%. The winner (17 s) passes. Q_TRANSITION_MS within 2% of the best cost: 14, 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17, 20 s.

Notes

Limitations

  • Back-transition: B1 and C. Forward transition: FT, when it is among the analyses; B1 does not cover it.
  • The forward transition in the energy budget is a quasi-steady estimate.
  • AIRSPEED_MIN: D, C, B1 and FT read it as an equivalent airspeed (D.entry_convention); Q2, which feeds E, reads it as an equivalent airspeed (Q2.feed_convention). Which one ArduPilot compares is open (O-02).
  • Input set is not release grade: 72 register entries are TBD: controller.altitude_hold.K_h, controller.altitude_hold.K_i, controller.altitude_hold.K_vh, controller.altitude_hold.i_max, controller.altitude_hold.v_dem_max, controller.ardupilot.AIRSPEED_MIN, ... (72 in all)
